info.title: Samva API
info.description: Samva is the email API for your app. Send transactional email in one typed call. Delivery events and customer replies come back as signed webhooks, and replies thread to the email they answer.

schema.description: Only this namespace's messages. A key scoped to a namespace always lists its own.

get.description: Returns message summaries, newest first (oldest first when filtered by conversation), with optional filters for channel, direction, status, conversation, contact, sender address, and creation time. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

anyOf.description: Optional org-scoped key that makes a send idempotent. Repeating a request with the same key and identical payload replays the original 201 response; reusing the key with different content returns 409.

post.description: Sends a message on the requested channel and returns its receipt (id, status, and why it waits when it does) with a 201 Created status. Requires `messages:create` or the send permission of the channel it sends on, such as `email:send`. `channel` selects the payload variant. Repeating an identical request with the same optional `Idempotency-Key` header returns the original receipt; reusing the key for different content returns a conflict.

get.description: Returns a message by its ID: addresses, subject, status, and why it is waiting when it is. Per-recipient delivery state and the body are their own reads.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a message by its ID.

get.description: Returns one delivery per recipient: its status, attempts, delivery times, and why it failed or is waiting.
Returns the content the message was sent or received with.

receivedAt.description: When Samva's receiving server accepted the email; null for outbound email. The sender's `Date` header plays no part and stays in the raw MIME.

get.description: Returns email delivery details for a message, optionally including signed URLs for its raw MIME, HTML, and text content.

post.description: Resolves recipients, sender, and inline or published-template content without sending anything, creating contacts or messages, or counting toward your quota.

get.description: Returns the current delivery status of a message by its ID.
Returns the delivery events recorded for a message, oldest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Lists asynchronous operations for the active organization, newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns one asynchronous operation from the active organization.

post.description: Retries a failed operation in place when its error is retryable. Retrying an organization deletion additionally requires `organization:delete`.

Schedules a message for dispatch at the absolute ISO-8601 timestamp supplied in scheduledFor. Requires `messages:create` or the send permission of the channel it sends on, such as `email:send`. Optional timezone is validated IANA display metadata only and never changes the execution instant.

get.description: Returns scheduled messages, soonest send first, optionally filtered by status. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns a single scheduled message by its ID.

post.description: Cancels a pending scheduled message so it will not be sent, and returns the updated scheduled message.
Explicitly resumes a scheduled message after onboarding review clearance. An overdue message requires either send_now or a new future scheduledFor value.
Creates an email campaign draft for the given audience and content, returning the created campaign.

get.description: Returns the organization's campaigns, newest first, optionally filtered by status. Each row carries `series`, the last 14 days of daily email sends the campaign produced, oldest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns a single campaign, including its content, audience, and policy, by its identifier.

patch.description: Updates the name, content, audience, or policy of a campaign draft.

post.description: Archives a draft campaign so it can no longer be scheduled, returning the archived campaign.

Schedules an email campaign run at the absolute ISO-8601 instant in scheduledFor, or immediately when omitted. The optional idempotencyKey is scoped to the organization and replays return the original run. An email campaign must carry the brand footer: it is refused with CampaignFooterRequiredError when its footer is off and its template renders no BrandFooter, and with BrandAddressRequiredError when a brand that signs it off has no postal address.

get.description: Returns a campaign's runs, newest first, optionally filtered by status. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns a single run of a campaign by its identifier.

post.description: Pauses an in-progress campaign run and returns the updated run.
Resumes a paused campaign run and returns the updated run.
Best-effort cancellation: pending recipients are skipped, while deliveries already handed off for sending may finish. Returns the updated run.

get.description: Returns a campaign run's recipients in the order the run admitted them, optionally filtered by status. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

Returns the customer-safe organization review decision, workflow stage, next action, and current sending-identity clearances. An organization that has not been reviewed yet is returned in the blocked initial state.

post.description: Allows an organization owner or admin to submit a rejected organization for review again. The expected generation prevents acting on stale status.
Allows organization owners and admins to submit a text response and up to three evidence uploads for the current information request.
post.summary: Respond to an email onboarding information request

get.description: Returns the organization's independent defaults for open and click tracking, both enabled unless configured otherwise. Recipient opt-out takes precedence over these defaults.

patch.description: Updates one or both organization email tracking defaults and returns the complete saved policy. Recipient opt-out still takes precedence.

get.description: Returns the organization-scoped tracking opt-out for a normalized recipient email. A missing preference reads as opted in and is not created.

patch.description: Opts a normalized recipient email in or out of open and click tracking. Opt-out takes precedence over per-send overrides and organization defaults without changing suppression or send eligibility.

post.description: Registers a domain for sending and returns it with the DNS records required to verify ownership and configure DKIM. Responds with 201. Supplying a connection attaches the domain to that DNS account; the domain must sit inside the zone given with it. When Samva cannot register another sending domain right now, this responds with 429 and no domain is created. A banned organization is refused with 403. `namespaceId` places the domain in a namespace, and only that namespace's keys and organization-wide callers reach it; a namespace-scoped key always adds to its own namespace.

get.description: Returns the organization's sending domains, newest first. A namespace-scoped key lists only its namespace's domains; an organization-wide caller lists every domain, or one namespace's with `namespaceId`. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. `sendable=true` lists only domains a send can use now: active, and verified, or verified before and degraded since. Each row carries `deliverability` (bounce and complaint rates over the last 24 hours, the window the 5% bounce limit is enforced over) and `series`, the last 14 days of daily email sends attributed to the domain, oldest first.
Returns the domain's last observed DNS and verification state. Reading it does not check DNS again or change anything; use advance to check now.

post.description: Creates a new DKIM signing key and returns its public DKIM record. Publish it, then advance domain verification to switch signing to the new key. Keep the former record published at least until `minimumRetainUntil`.
Checks the required DNS records now and, once they all match, moves the domain toward verified. Safe to call repeatedly.

get.description: Returns a single sending domain, including its DNS records and verification details.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a sending domain from the organization.

post.description: Looks up the domain's nameservers to detect its DNS registrar and returns the provider, nameservers, and a link to its setup docs.

get.description: Reports whether the domain's DNS provider supports Domain Connect one-click setup for Samva, and the provider's name when it does. Ineligible is a normal result — the manual DNS records remain the way to verify.

post.description: Builds the signed Domain Connect apply URL for the selected sending-only or sending-and-receiving service. The sending-and-receiving service writes the apex inbound MX, so it is refused until the domain's receiving is enabled. Manual DNS remains available for either mode.
post.summary: Build a one-click DNS apply URL

post.description: Consumes the Domain Connect provider's redirect. Validates the signed state and, when the DNS provider reports success, starts checking the domain's records. A DNS provider error is reported separately from a customer cancelling setup.

Enables inbound receiving for a verified domain and returns the recipient addresses it accepts. Set `catchAll` to route every address on the domain; that needs a destination: a webhook endpoint, supplied as `endpointId` or already configured on the domain, or at least one active forwarding rule that covers the domain. Mail that matches neither is rejected, never accepted and dropped.
post.summary: Enable inbound email for a domain

get.description: Reports each prerequisite for receiving a domain's mail at Samva, in order: sending verified, a destination (a webhook endpoint or an active forwarding rule), receiving enabled, and the inbound MX record. The MX answer is a live DNS lookup that names the current target when mail is routed elsewhere.

post.description: Marks a verified domain as the organization's default sending domain, atomically clearing any previous default. Provisioning and inbound routing prefer the default domain when several apply. It does not choose the `from` of omitted-`from` sends; those use the organization default sender.

patch.description: Overrides the domain's open/click tracking, reply-to, unsubscribe-group defaults, and the brand its mail uses for the settings cascade. An omitted field is left unchanged; null clears it back to the organization default. Returns the saved config.

post.description: Provisions a custom tracking domain (default label `track`) for a verified sending domain so open/click links redirect through the customer's own subdomain. Requires a plan that includes custom tracking domains. Returns the resulting state including the two DNS records the customer must create.

get.description: Returns the custom tracking state for a sending domain: lifecycle status, the required DNS records, certificate and CAA readiness, and any scheduled teardown. `enabled` is false when no custom tracking domain is provisioned.

delete.description: Disables a domain's custom tracking, removes its managed resources, and immediately returns sends to the shared tracking host. Existing custom links in already-delivered mail stop working.

post.description: Checks the hostname's certificate now instead of waiting for the next scheduled check, and returns the refreshed state. Samva checks a hostname at most once every 30 seconds; a recheck inside that window returns the state from the last check. Returns a conflict when custom tracking is disabled or being torn down.
post.summary: Recheck a custom tracking domain's certificate

get.description: Reports whether the domain's DNS provider supports Domain Connect for its current Custom Tracking Domain. Ineligible is a normal result and the exact manual CNAME records remain available.
get.summary: Check automatic Custom Tracking Domain setup eligibility

post.description: Builds the signed Domain Connect URL for the current customer-selected tracking host. Samva fills in the host and the certificate validation record; the manual CNAME records remain available.
post.summary: Build an automatic Custom Tracking Domain apply URL

post.description: Validates the signed state returned by the DNS provider, then checks the tracking host again. Returning here never marks the host ready or changes which tracking host email uses.
post.summary: Complete an automatic Custom Tracking Domain return

post.description: Creates a sender. A sender on a domain takes the domain's namespace, and a `namespaceId` that names another namespace is refused; a sender with no domain joins `namespaceId`, or its key's namespace. A namespace-scoped key cannot add a sender on a domain outside its namespace. The required Idempotency-Key replays the original sender for an identical request and conflicts when reused with different input.

get.description: Returns senders, newest first. A namespace-scoped key lists only its namespace's senders; an organization-wide caller lists every sender, or one namespace's with `namespaceId`. Optionally filtered by verification status, active state, or default flag. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Each row carries `deliverability` (bounce and complaint rates over the last 24 hours) and `series`, the last 14 days of daily email sends from the address, oldest first.
Returns the current verification status of a sender.

namespaceId.description: The namespace the sender belongs to, or null at organization level. A sender on a domain takes the domain's namespace.

get.description: Returns one sender owned by the authenticated organization. Other organizations' ids are reported as not found.

delete.description: Accepts sender removal and marks the sender inactive. A default sender can be removed when no other active sender remains in the organization. It reports the `deleting` lifecycle until removal finishes.

post.description: Marks a verified, active sender as the default of its scope, atomically clearing the previous default of the same scope: the organization level, or the sender's namespace. Omitted-`from` sends use it when neither the request nor the template names a `from`; with no default, the organization's sole verified sender is used.

get.description: Returns aggregate email statistics — sent, delivered, bounced, and complained counts with their rates — optionally scoped to messages created from `after` (inclusive) to `before` (exclusive).

post.description: Enables catch-all inbound receiving for a verified domain. `endpointId` is one of the organization's webhook endpoints; every address on the domain delivers `message.received` to it. Omit it to deliver through forwarding rules alone, which needs at least one active forwarding rule covering the domain. Mail that matches neither a rule nor an endpoint is rejected as an unknown recipient. Responds with 201.
Disables catch-all inbound receiving for a domain.

patch.description: Updates a domain's catch-all receiving configuration: the webhook endpoint that receives its inbound mail.

get.description: Returns the catch-all receiving configuration for a domain, including the webhook endpoint that receives its inbound mail and its email counts.
Returns catch-all receiving counters for a domain, adding an aggregated breakdown when `after` or `before` bounds a range: `after` inclusive, `before` exclusive.

Returns the addresses this organization will not send to, newest first, optionally filtered by suppression type, active or expired state, and an address substring. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns how many addresses this organization will not send to now, by suppression type. Expired suppressions are not counted.

delete.description: Deletes a suppression so this organization can send to the address again. If the deletion cannot complete, it fails rather than reporting success, and it is safe to retry. Deliverability caveat: a bounce or complaint suppression records a real delivery failure, and sending to the address again risks the reputation damage the suppression prevented.

post.description: Blocks an email address or domain from inbound receiving and returns the created block entry. Responds with 201.

get.description: Returns block entries, newest first, optionally filtered by block type and active state. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a block entry, unblocking the associated address or domain.

patch.description: Updates a block entry's reason, notes, active state, or expiry.

get.description: Returns inbound emails that were blocked, most recently blocked first, optionally filtered by block entry, sender, or block time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

post.description: Checks whether an email address is currently blocked and returns the matching block rule when one applies.
post.summary: Check whether an address is blocked

post.description: Creates an inbound email forwarding rule and returns it. Responds with 201. Priority is a non-negative integer, default 0; higher priority rules are tried first, and at equal priority an exact address outranks a wildcard pattern. An organization holds at most 100 forwarding rules.

get.description: Returns every inbound email forwarding rule in the order inbound mail is matched against them: highest priority first, then an exact address before a wildcard pattern at equal priority, then oldest first. The first rule that matches is the one that forwards. Filtering by domain returns that domain's rules and the rules that apply to every domain (domainId null). An organization holds at most 100, so the list is never paged.

patch.description: Updates an inbound email forwarding rule and returns its current summary.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an inbound email forwarding rule.

get.description: Returns forwarded inbound emails with their delivery outcomes, newest first, optionally filtered by rule, status, or creation time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

Returns the domain's automated warming policy, its system-created 24-hour windows and policy snapshots, the rolling bounce and complaint window the safety rule reads, every pause above the plan, and the decision history. A domain without a plan returns the evidence and a null plan.

post.description: Starts an automated warming policy on a verified sending domain. Samva opens the first 24-hour campaign window immediately, then opens later windows from the saved growth policy after safe windows close. Direct sends are counted in the domain's window but never delayed. Responds with 201.

patch.description: Updates the growth percentage and daily target Samva uses for future 24-hour warming windows. Existing windows keep their policy snapshot, including a scheduled window, so prior authorization remains auditable.

delete.description: Cancels a scheduled or open system-created warming window. Recipients a campaign run already reserved from it stay reserved; no further runs draw from it.

post.description: Pauses the plan. Campaign runs from the domain stop at their next page and queued campaign email waits until it expires; direct sends are unaffected.

Resumes a paused or held plan and the campaign runs it was holding. A plan the domain rule held resumes only once the domain's rolling window is under both limits again; until then the request is refused with the observed rate.
Ends the policy. Campaign runs from the domain are no longer gated by warming windows; the organization safeguards still apply.

Creates the media object in the pending state and returns it with the upload instruction — URL, method, and headers — for putting its bytes into storage. Requires `messages:create`, or `email:send` for `attachment` media.
post.x-samva-scope: messages:create or email:send or mailboxes:send or mailboxes:update

post.description: Verifies the uploaded object exists in storage, marks the media object ready, and returns it with a download URL. Requires the permission that creating the media object did.
post.x-samva-scope: messages:create or email:send or mailboxes:send or mailboxes:update

delete.description: Deletes a pending media object and the bytes stored for it. Fails if the media object is already ready.

get.description: Returns the media object's metadata, including status, dimensions, and confirmation timestamps.
Generates a presigned, time-limited download URL for a ready media object.
Returns metadata for a single attachment, including filename, content type, and size.

delete.description: Deletes an attachment and returns the deleted attachment's ID.

get.description: Returns every attachment of the given message, newest first. A message's attachments all ride that one email, so the list is never paged.
Generates a presigned, time-limited download URL for the attachment; expiry is configurable via the expiresIn query parameter.

Returns conversation summaries, most recently active first, filterable by status, channel, contact, and creation time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. A conversation that gains activity while you page moves ahead of the cursor, so a walk lists each conversation at most once. Read a conversation's contacts, metadata, and resolution with `GET /v1/conversations/{id}`.

post.description: Creates a new conversation with its initial contacts and returns it with a 201 status.

get.description: Returns a single conversation with the contacts taking part in it.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. `metadata` merges into the stored metadata by key, and a `null` value deletes that key. `primaryChannel` must be one of the conversation's channels. Tags, categories, and channels are not updated here: use `POST` and `DELETE` on `/v1/conversations/{id}/tags`, `/v1/conversations/{id}/categories`, and `/v1/conversations/{id}/channels`.

get.description: Returns the conversation's message summaries, oldest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read a message's content with `GET /v1/messages/{id}/content`.

post.description: Adds the given tags to the conversation, keeping the tags it already has, and returns the conversation.

delete.description: Removes the given tags from the conversation and returns the conversation. A tag the conversation does not have is ignored.

post.description: Adds the given categories to the conversation, keeping the ones it already has, and returns the conversation.

delete.description: Removes the given categories from the conversation and returns the conversation. A category the conversation does not have is ignored.

post.description: Adds the given channels to the conversation, keeping the ones it already has, and returns the conversation.

delete.description: Removes the given channels from the conversation and returns the conversation. The primary channel cannot be removed; a channel the conversation does not have is ignored.

post.description: Attaches one or more contacts to a conversation and returns the updated conversation.

delete.description: Detaches one or more contacts from a conversation and returns the updated conversation.

get.description: Returns contact summaries for the organization, newest first, filterable by search term, status, and creation time (`after`, `before`). `fields` is a comma-separated list of defined custom field keys to return in each summary's `customFields`; omitted keys and unselected fields are not returned. Filter by one defined custom field with `customField` and a JSON-encoded scalar `customFieldValue` (for example, `"creator"`, `42`, or `true`). Both filter parameters are required together, and unknown keys or values of the wrong type are rejected. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read full identities, profile, and metadata with `GET /v1/contacts/{id}`.

post.description: Creates a contact and returns it with a 201 status. An identity another contact already holds is a conflict.

Looks up a single contact by exactly one of email address, phone number, or external ID and returns null when no contact matches. A phone number without `+` is read in the organization's default region.

Looks up exactly one identifier through `lookup: { type, value }`. Returns `{ contact, created: false }` unchanged when it exists. Otherwise creates the lookup identity (or external ID), applies `create` attributes, and returns `{ contact, created: true }`. Additional addresses belong in `create.identities`, custom fields in `create.profile.customFields`; custom field keys must be defined and values must match their types. An external ID lookup cannot be contradicted by `create.externalId`. Creation returns HTTP 409 ConflictError if an externalId or address belongs to another contact; the conflicting field is named and no contact is created. Use the update endpoint to change an existing contact.

get.description: Returns a contact with its identities, profile, tags, and metadata.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. `metadata` merges into the stored metadata by key, and a `null` value deletes that key. `profile` replaces each field it names and `null` clears one; its `customFields` merge by key the same way. Identities and tags are not updated here: use `POST /v1/contacts/{id}/identities`, `DELETE /v1/contacts/{id}/identities/{identityId}`, `POST /v1/contacts/{id}/tags`, and `DELETE /v1/contacts/{id}/tags`.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a contact by its ID.

post.description: Adds an address the contact is reached at and returns the contact. Adding an address the contact already has updates whether it is verified. An address another contact holds is a conflict.

delete.description: Removes one address from the contact and returns the contact.

put.description: Records the contact's consent on one channel at one of its addresses and returns the contact. `opted_out` stops every send on that channel to that address until the contact opts back in; `opted_in` is what channels that require opt-in check for. `source` and `capturedAt` say where and when the contact decided; `proof` keeps your evidence. A decision captured before the recorded one is ignored. A change publishes `contact.consent_changed`.

post.description: Adds the given tags to the contact, keeping the tags it already has, and returns the contact.

delete.description: Removes the given tags from the contact and returns the contact. A tag the contact does not have is ignored.

get.description: Returns aggregated engagement metrics for a contact, including message counts and active conversation totals.

post.description: Creates contacts in bulk from a list of entries shaped like a create request, returning per-entry results with created, updated, skipped, and error counts. An entry whose identities match an existing contact is skipped, or updates it with `onConflict: "update"`.
Permanently deletes multiple contacts by ID, returning counts of deleted and failed records.
Adds, removes, or replaces tags on multiple contacts in one request, returning counts of updated and failed records.
Sets the status on multiple contacts in one request, returning counts of updated and failed records.
Exports contacts as JSON or CSV, returning the serialized data and a count of exported records.

get.description: Returns a contact's message activity, newest first, optionally filtered by channel. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns the contact groups a contact belongs to, most recently joined first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

post.description: Records a custom contact event. Identify the contact by exactly one ID, external ID, or email. A missing email or external ID creates a contact; an unknown contact ID returns 404. An organization-scoped idempotency key replays the original event. Event names use letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, and dots, up to 255 characters; contact. and samva. prefixes are reserved. Properties allow at most 50 keys and 32 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Events are retained for 90 days.

Validates the full request shape, contact references, and event names before processing. A schema failure rejects the entire batch without writes. Between 1 and 100 valid entries are then processed in input order, with independent indexed results for properties limits, contact resolution, and idempotency.
post.summary: Record contact events in a batch

get.description: Returns custom and Samva lifecycle events, newest occurrence first, within the 90-day retention window. Pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page.
Returns the organization's journeys, newest first, optionally filtered by status. Pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page.

post.description: Creates a draft journey from a definition: a trigger, a root node, and a graph of at most 200 nodes that is acyclic and fully reachable. Templates, senders, and groups the definition names must belong to the organization. Requires a plan that includes journeys.

get.description: Returns a journey with its draft definition, its current revision, and its newest published version number.

patch.description: Renames a journey.

delete.description: Deletes a journey that was never published or is archived, with its versions and runs. An active or paused journey returns 409; archive it first.

put.description: Replaces the draft definition and returns the journey with a new revision. The request names the revision it read; a stale revision returns 409. Published versions and the runs on them do not change.

post.description: Publishes the draft as the next immutable version; new runs start on it and existing runs stay on the version they entered. The request names the revision it read; a stale revision returns 409. Publishing a draft identical to the newest version changes nothing. A draft journey becomes active; a paused journey stays paused. A published version sends and updates tags as its publisher, so a draft with a send_email node requires a key that can send email and one with an update_tags node requires contacts:update; without them the request returns 403.
Stops new enrollment and holds every live run before its next node, including a run whose wait ends while the journey is paused. Held runs report status paused.
Resumes enrollment and continues the runs the pause held. Requires a plan that includes journeys.
Stops new enrollment for good and exits every live run with exit reason archived. An archived journey cannot be edited, published, or resumed.

get.description: Returns the immutable definition of one published version.
Counts one published version's runs by status, and per node the live runs there now and the runs that have entered it. Defaults to the newest published version.
Returns a journey's runs, newest first, optionally filtered by status or contact. Pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page.
Returns one run with every node it entered, in order: when it entered and left, how it left, and the message a send node created.

post.description: Sends a confirmation email from your sender. Only the recipient's explicit confirmation adds them to the active static contact group and clears the optional unsubscribe group. The link expires after seven days and can be used once. A custom published email template receives confirmUrl. Sending follows ordinary sender, admission, billing, and brand-footer settings. Requires email send authority in addition to the declared contact grants, including the optional unsubscribe preference change.

get.description: Returns the organization's contact groups, newest first, filterable by type and active state. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

color.description: The list's label color, one of six families, or null for the neutral chip. Customer-chosen and purely presentational; it carries no meaning the API enforces.

post.description: Creates a new contact group and returns it with a 201 status.

anyOf.description: The list's label color, one of six families, or null for the neutral chip. Customer-chosen and purely presentational; it carries no meaning the API enforces.

color.description: The list's label color, one of six families, or null for the neutral chip. Customer-chosen and purely presentational; it carries no meaning the API enforces.

get.description: Returns a single contact group by its ID.

color.description: The list's label color, one of six families, or null for the neutral chip. Customer-chosen and purely presentational; it carries no meaning the API enforces.

patch.description: Updates an existing contact group's fields and returns the updated group.

anyOf.description: The list's label color, one of six families, or null for the neutral chip. Customer-chosen and purely presentational; it carries no meaning the API enforces.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a contact group by its ID.

post.description: Adds one or more contacts to a contact group, returning counts of added and skipped members.
post.summary: Add members to a contact group

delete.description: Removes one or more contacts from a contact group, returning the count of removed members.
delete.summary: Remove members from a contact group

get.description: Returns a contact group's members, most recently joined first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
get.summary: List members of a contact group

post.description: Recomputes a dynamic contact group's membership from its criteria, returning counts of added, removed, and total members.
Evaluates group criteria without persisting, returning the matching contact count and a sample of matches.

get.description: Returns every custom field definition for the organization in display order. An organization defines at most 100, so the list is never paged.

post.description: Creates a new custom field definition and returns it with a 201 status; the field key must be unique, and an organization defines at most 100.

patch.description: Updates an existing custom field definition and returns the updated field.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom field definition by its ID.

get.description: Returns every unsubscribe group in the organization, the default group first, then by name. An organization holds at most 200, so the list is never paged.

post.description: Creates a new unsubscribe group and returns it with a 201 Created status. An organization holds at most 200 groups.

patch.description: Updates the name or description of an unsubscribe group.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an unsubscribe group by its ID. The default group cannot be deleted; make another group the default first. A group a scheduled or running campaign uses cannot be deleted until that run finishes or is cancelled.

post.description: Makes this group the organization's default: campaigns that name no group, and whose template and sending domain name none, unsubscribe recipients from it.
post.summary: Make an unsubscribe group the default

post.description: Moves contacts out of an unsubscribe group's audience and returns the number added and the number skipped. Leaving a group stops that group's sends to the contact on every channel. Each member is a contact ID, an email address, or a phone number; an address no contact holds gets a new contact, so an import from another email service needs no contacts first.
post.summary: Add contacts to an unsubscribe group

delete.description: Returns contacts to an unsubscribe group's audience and returns the number removed. Each member is a contact ID, an email address, or a phone number; an address no contact holds is skipped.
delete.summary: Remove contacts from an unsubscribe group

get.description: Returns the contacts that have left an unsubscribe group, newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

Returns the unsubscribe groups a contact has left, optionally limited to a specified set of groups. Name the contact by exactly one of `contactId`, `email`, or `phone`. Membership belongs to the contact, so the answer is the same whichever identifier names it; `contactId` is null, and no groups are returned, when no contact holds the email or phone.

Returns outbound message counts over the half-open selected instant range, grouped by organization-local calendar day, week, or month. A range with traffic returns every bucket in it, including the ones that saw none; a range with no outbound traffic at all returns no buckets. A range with no `before` runs through the current instant, so its quiet trailing buckets are reported as zero.

Returns aggregate delivery metrics plus unique-message email Open and Click rates over the selected date range. `sent` counts every outbound message accepted in the range; each rate is taken over the messages the channel actually attempted, so one still waiting to be sent neither helps nor hurts it. Each engagement rate uses the corresponding tracking-eligible delivered-message cohort; repeated provider observations do not inflate the numerator.

Returns the contacts your organization exchanged the most messages with over the selected date range. `sortBy` chooses the traffic `messageCount` reports and ranks by: `sent` counts outbound messages addressed to the contact, `received` counts inbound messages the contact sent you, and `total` (the default) counts both. Contacts with no traffic in the range are omitted, and at most 100 are returned.
get.summary: List top contacts by message volume

get.description: Returns outbound message counts over the half-open selected instant range, bucketed by organization-local hour. Empty ranges return no rows; non-empty ranges include all 24 hours.

Returns delivered, failed, and pending rates plus average delivery time for the outbound messages accepted in the selected date range, optionally filtered by channel. Every accepted message falls into exactly one of the three, so they always sum to 100%: a complaint counts as delivered because the message arrived, a bounce counts as failed, and anything the provider has not resolved yet counts as pending. Mail your organization received is not rated here.

post.description: Exports one record per outbound message accepted in the given date range as CSV or JSON and returns the file content inline. CSV follows RFC 4180: fields containing a quote, comma, or line break are quoted with embedded quotes doubled, and records are separated by CRLF. At most 10,000 records are returned, newest first.

schema.description: Only templates in this namespace. A namespace-scoped key lists its own namespace's templates only.

get.description: Returns template summaries, newest first, filterable by category, channel, status, project, and search. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read a template's compiled content, current publication, and input schema with `GET /v1/templates/{id}`.

post.description: Creates an email template project from Samva's canonical TSX starter and returns its template entry with status 201.

get.description: Returns the organization's template families with their members, newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

post.description: Creates an empty template family with the supplied name and returns it with status 201.

get.description: Returns a template family and its channel-specific member templates.

patch.description: Changes a template family's name and returns the updated family.

delete.description: Deletes a template family without deleting its member templates.

post.description: Creates a template family containing the specified template and returns the new family with status 201.
post.summary: Create a family from a template

post.description: Adds an existing template as a channel member of the family and returns the updated family.
post.summary: Attach a template to a family

delete.description: Removes a member template from the family without deleting the template.
delete.summary: Detach a template from a family

get.description: Returns the template with its project entry path, delivery defaults, compiled channel content, current publication, and the input schema that publication validates against. Open live project files through the workspace API.

patch.description: Updates template metadata. Setting `entryPath` points the template at another file in its project and keeps its id, slug, and publications; move the file in Git separately. Source changes use the project workspace API.

delete.description: Deletes a template from the organization and returns a success flag.

post.description: Registers a `.tsx` file under `templates/` or `emails/` in an existing template project as its own template and returns it with status 201. The file does not need to exist yet; publishing fails until a commit contains it. Repeating the call with the same entry path, name, and slug returns the existing template.
Creates or opens the shared project workspace at the latest saved version and returns its effective files.

patch.description: Applies revision-checked file patches to the shared project workspace overlay.

post.description: Returns exact added, modified, and deleted project files against the current Git base commit.

put.description: Writes one image or font (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, or woff2) into the shared project workspace as an unsaved file; Save commits it. The JSON body carries the file as canonical base64 in `contentBase64`, at most 1 MiB decoded, and the bytes must match the extension in `path`. `replace` must be `false` to add a new file and `true` to change an existing one.

post.description: Resolves one conflicted file by keeping the draft, using main, or supplying edited source.
Validates the effective project tree and saves it as one Git commit on the template repository's default branch.
Builds the template entry before atomically staging a reachable historical commit and its emitted source; a later Save appends a new commit without rewriting branch history.
post.summary: Stage a historical template project tree

get.description: Returns recent history from the template repository's default branch.

post.description: Builds the template entry from the current effective workspace tree, including unsaved file patches, and returns what the template declares plus every compile and target-client finding. Nothing is written and no message is rendered.
Renders one of the named inputs the template declares against the current effective workspace tree. Only declared fixtures render here; arbitrary input renders against a publication.
post.summary: Render a declared template workspace fixture

post.description: Builds an exact Git commit and entry path, stores the immutable compiled IR and its assets, records the input contract it validates against, and makes that publication current. A commit that compiles to the same build as an existing publication makes that publication current again instead of recording another.

get.description: Returns one immutable publication and its exact build receipt.

post.description: Renders one immutable publication against the `data` you pass, formatted in the `locale` and `timeZone` you name as a send formats them, and returns the subject, preheader, HTML and plain text a send would produce. `data` is validated against the publication's input schema exactly as a send validates it; invalid input returns a validation error that names each failing field. Nothing is sent or stored. Unpublished workspace edits are never rendered: only a publication id renders.

get.description: Returns the immutable input contracts this template has published under, newest version first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Send against a contract to follow later publications that validate input identically.
Returns one immutable input contract and the published schema it validates against.
Returns the credential-free HTTPS remote and default branch for the template project repository.
get.summary: Get a template project Git repository

post.description: Exchanges the caller's Samva authorization for a one-hour Git credential scoped to the template repository.
post.summary: Issue a template project Git credential

post.description: Adds or replaces one bounded persistent read-only resource and advances the workspace revision.
Removes one persistent resource from mounted context and advances the workspace revision.

get.description: Returns the organization's brands, the default brand first.

post.description: Creates a brand. The CSS must parse as a brand theme; a rejected theme answers 422 with located findings under `fields.css`. With `isDefault`, the new brand becomes the default. An organization holds at most 12 brands; creating one more answers 409 with a `ConflictError`.

get.description: Returns one brand by its slug.

patch.description: Updates a brand. Each section given replaces that section whole. Published templates keep the brand they were built against until they are republished.

delete.description: Deletes a brand. The default brand cannot be deleted; domains that used the deleted brand fall back to the default.

post.description: Makes this brand the organization's default: bare `samva:brand` and domains without a brand resolve to it at their next build or send.

Creates a signed webhook endpoint for Samva delivery and inbound events, stores subscriptions, and returns the endpoint and signing secret with a 201 response. `namespaceId` confines the endpoint to one namespace's events and `mailboxIds` to those mailboxes' events; when both are set, every mailbox must belong to the namespace.

get.description: Returns the organization's webhook endpoints, oldest first, with each endpoint's delivery counts, optionally filtered by a search term matched against name and URL, and by status. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns the configuration of the webhook endpoint with the given ID.

patch.description: Updates a webhook's name, URL, subscribed events, channels, custom headers, mailbox scope, or status and returns the updated endpoint. A change to `mailboxIds` or `namespaceId` is checked as the endpoint will stand afterward: every mailbox must belong to the namespace when both are set.

delete.description: Deletes a webhook endpoint so it no longer receives event deliveries.

post.description: Queues a signed webhook.test event through the normal delivery and retry lifecycle.

get.description: Returns a webhook endpoint's deliveries, newest first, each naming the event type and time it was made for, with its nested attempt diagnostics. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

Returns aggregate pending, delivered, exhausted, and cancelled delivery counts for a webhook endpoint over its whole retained history, plus the same counts per organization-local calendar day between `after` and `before`, a window of at most 90 days that defaults to the last 30 days. Deliveries are retained for 90 days, so the longest window is the whole history.

post.description: Performs one immediate manual redelivery attempt and returns that attempt's identity and outcome without changing the automatic retry lifecycle.
Generates and returns a new signing secret. The previous secret remains valid for a 24-hour rotation overlap.
Creates a new organization under the current billing account and returns it.

get.description: Returns the organization for the current billing account.

patch.description: Updates the current organization's profile, regional defaults, and reply-to default and returns the saved organization. `metadata` is merged into the stored value; every other field is replaced.

id.description: Opaque identity for your organization membership

nickname.description: Your display name and organization name

get.description: Returns your identity in the organization authorized by your credential. The ID remains stable across reconnects and display-name changes. Removing and re-adding your membership creates a new ID.

Returns the current trust tier, plan and probation sending limits, and measured probation graduation progress. Limits are additional to billing allowance, domain readiness, and enforcement. Graduation is evaluated on delivery events.
get.summary: Get organization trust tier and sending limits

get.description: Returns usage statistics for the current organization between `after` and `before`, which default to the current calendar month so far. `usage.periodStart` and `usage.periodEnd` echo the window counted.

post.description: Starts an owner-authorized organization deletion operation, confirming the organization name in the request. Repeating the same request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the existing organization-scoped operation.
Creates a new API key for the organization and returns the created key, including the plaintext secret, with a 201 response.

access.description: Defaults to full access. A restricted API key creating a key defaults to its own grants and cannot issue full access.

get.description: Returns the organization's API keys, newest first, filterable by status and a search term matched against name and description. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns the API key with the given ID, including its metadata and access.

patch.description: Updates an API key's settings and returns the updated key. A field left out keeps its value.

mailboxes.description: Changes the mailbox send mode of a key that holds mailbox access. Only a person can change it; the change applies to the key's next request.

post.description: Deactivates an API key so it can no longer authenticate requests. Revocation is final: a revoked key never authenticates again. Its record stays listable, so the messages it sent stay attributed to it.
Issues a replacement with the same owner, name, and access, then deactivates the existing key. Returns the new key, including the plaintext secret.

get.description: Returns aggregate send counts and daily volume attributed to an API key between `after` and `before`, a window of at most 90 days that defaults to the last 30 days.
Returns the sends attributed to an API key, newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

post.description: Tells Samva what was confusing, broken, or missing in the API. Programs and coding agents can call it the moment something goes wrong, naming the operation and resource involved. Samva's team reads every report; the answer is a receipt, not a reply.

get.description: Returns the organization the request acts in and the credential it presents: an API key with its name, prefix, and access, or a signed-in user with their role. Any valid credential may call it, whatever its grants.

Returns summaries of the mailboxes the caller can read, newest first, filterable by creation time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read a mailbox's endpoints and metadata with `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}`.

post.description: Creates a mailbox with one endpoint and returns it with status 201; the caller gets an admin grant on it. An email endpoint's address must be under the organization's Samva-hosted mail domain or a verified domain with receiving enabled, and the mailbox sends from it. A phone endpoint's address is a number the organization connected on that channel, in E.164 form. The slug defaults to the address's local part, or a phone number's digits. Pass `slug` when that is taken or not a valid slug. The mailbox receives mail from now on; mail that arrived earlier is not added to it. Conflicts if the address or slug is already in use. Returns 402 when the organization is at its plan's mailbox allowance or at its mailbox storage allowance; incoming mail is still received past the storage allowance.

get.description: Returns a mailbox with its endpoints and metadata; each endpoint says whether it is the mailbox's default on its channel. Its grants are `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/grants` and its send policies `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/policies`.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. `metadata` merges into the stored metadata by key, and a `null` value deletes that key. Change an endpoint's sender name or default with `PATCH /v1/mailboxes/{id}/endpoints/{endpointId}`.

delete.description: Deletes a mailbox with its endpoints, threads, drafts, and history. The messages it received stay with the organization. The mailbox leaves every API key scope and webhook endpoint filter that named it; a key or endpoint left with no mailbox is disabled.

post.description: Adds an endpoint to a mailbox and returns the mailbox with status 201. It follows the same rules as the endpoint of a new mailbox: an email address must be under the organization's Samva-hosted mail domain or a verified domain with receiving enabled, a phone number must be one the organization connected on that channel, and no mailbox may already hold it (409). Messages sent to it reach the mailbox from now on. It becomes the default on its channel only when the mailbox has no endpoint there yet.
post.summary: Add an endpoint to a mailbox

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest, and returns the mailbox. `displayName` is the name messages sent from the endpoint carry; null falls back to the mailbox's name. `default: true` makes the endpoint the one the mailbox starts new conversations from on its channel; replies always leave from the endpoint of their thread.

delete.description: Removes an endpoint from a mailbox and returns the mailbox. Messages sent to it stop reaching the mailbox; its existing threads and messages stay, and replies in them leave from the mailbox's default endpoint on their channel. A mailbox keeps at least one endpoint, so removing the last one is refused (422). When the removed endpoint was the default on its channel, the oldest remaining endpoint there becomes the default.
delete.summary: Remove an endpoint from a mailbox

post.description: Stops the mailbox sending and stops new inbound mail reaching it. Mail that arrives while it is paused is not added when it resumes. Resume it with `POST /v1/mailboxes/{id}/resume`.
Lets a paused mailbox send and receive again.

get.description: Counts the actions proposed and events recorded on a mailbox between `after` and `before` (omit both for all time), and the sends waiting for approval now. List the actions and events themselves with `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/actions` and `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/events`.
Returns who can use the mailbox, what each grant allows, and whether its sends wait for approval, newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

post.description: Shares a mailbox with an organization member and returns the grant with status 201. The member must already belong to the organization. A member who already holds a grant conflicts rather than being rewritten: change an existing grant with `PATCH /v1/mailboxes/{id}/grants/{grantId}`, so a grant is never widened as a side effect of granting. List the current grants with `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/grants`.
post.summary: Grant a member access to a mailbox

patch.description: Changes a member's role, send mode, or both on a mailbox and returns the updated grant. A field left out keeps its value; naming neither is a validation error. Taking admin from the last grant that can configure the mailbox conflicts, as revoking it does. The change applies to the member's next request on every surface.

delete.description: Removes a member's access to a mailbox. The last grant that can configure the mailbox cannot be revoked, so a mailbox is never left with nobody able to administer it: grant a teammate the admin role before removing your own.

get.description: Returns every send policy on a mailbox, oldest first. A mailbox holds at most 20 policies, so the list is never paged. Each enabled policy holds (`requireApproval`) or refuses (`deny`) every send from the mailbox; `deny` wins when both apply.

post.description: Adds a send policy to a mailbox and returns it with status 201. It applies to every send proposed after it is created, whoever proposes it. A mailbox that already holds 20 policies conflicts.

get.description: Returns one send policy.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. Set `enabled` to `false` to stop a policy applying without deleting it.

delete.description: Deletes a send policy. Sends it already holds stay held until a person approves or denies them.

get.description: Returns each folder that holds a thread with its thread count and the caller's unread count. The folder set is fixed, so the list is never paged.
Returns every label defined on a mailbox, ordered by name. A mailbox holds at most 100 labels, so the list is never paged.

post.description: Creates a label on a mailbox and returns it with status 201. Slugs are unique within the mailbox, and a mailbox holds at most 100 labels; either limit conflicts.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest.

delete.description: Deletes a label and removes it from every thread that carries it.

get.description: Returns thread summaries, most recent activity first. `after` and `before` filter by last activity, so an agent polling for new mail passes the last time it looked. `q` is a full-text search over subjects, senders, and message text; `folder`, `label`, `unread`, and `starred` narrow the list. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. A thread that gains activity while you page moves ahead of the cursor, so a walk lists each thread at most once.
Returns a thread with its participants and where it stands. Read its messages with `GET .../threads/{threadId}/messages` and their bodies with `GET .../threads/{threadId}/content`.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. `folder` and `priority` are shared with everyone on the mailbox; `read`, `starred`, and `snoozedUntil` are the caller's own. Labels are not updated here: use `POST` and `DELETE` on `/v1/mailboxes/{id}/threads/{threadId}/labels`. Returns where the thread stands, not its messages: read those with `GET .../threads/{threadId}`.

post.description: Adds the given mailbox labels to the thread, keeping the labels it already has, and returns where the thread stands. Every id must be one of the mailbox's labels.

delete.description: Removes the given labels from the thread and returns where the thread stands. A label the thread does not carry is ignored.

get.description: Returns the thread's message summaries, oldest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read the bodies with `GET .../threads/{threadId}/content` or one message with `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/messages/{messageId}`.
get.summary: List messages in a mailbox thread

get.description: Returns the thread's messages with their text, sanitized HTML, `replyText` (what each sender wrote, without quoted history), authentication verdicts, and attachments, oldest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
Returns the internal notes on a thread with their bodies, oldest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.
get.summary: List notes in a mailbox thread

post.description: Adds an internal note to a thread and returns it with status 201. Notes are visible to everyone on the mailbox and never sent.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. Only the note's author may.

delete.description: Deletes a note. Only the note's author may.

anyOf.description: Optional key that makes a mailbox send idempotent for the calling key or member. Repeating the request with the same key and body returns the original action in its current state. Keep the key after a lost response. Reusing it with different content returns 409. Active actions retain their key; terminal receipts remain replayable for 24 hours.

post.description: Starts a new conversation from the mailbox's default endpoint on the channel the body names (email when omitted); a mailbox with no endpoint on that channel is refused (422). A message to a number joins the mailbox's thread with that number when it has one. Records a send action and returns 202 with its current receipt and a Location for action status. An installation, grant, or policy may require approval; otherwise the send is queued. Observe the same action through acceptance and mailbox completion. A policy refusal returns 403 with the recorded receipt.

get.description: Returns a message in the mailbox, discriminated by `channel`. An email has its text, sanitized HTML, `replyText` (what the sender wrote, without quoted history), authentication verdicts, and attachments.
Returns a short-lived URL for the message exactly as it was received (`message/rfc822`). Sent messages have no stored MIME.
Returns a short-lived download URL for one of the message's attachments.

post.description: Copies one of a received message's attachments into the organization's media and returns it as a draft attachment (`mediaId`), so a draft can carry it. A draft that forwards a message saves each original attachment this way.

anyOf.description: Optional key that makes a mailbox send idempotent for the calling key or member. Repeating the request with the same key and body returns the original action in its current state. Keep the key after a lost response. Reusing it with different content returns 409. Active actions retain their key; terminal receipts remain replayable for 24 hours.

post.description: Replies to the message's Reply-To address, or its sender, in the same thread and from the thread's endpoint. The server sets the recipients, subject, and threading headers. The body's `channel` must match the thread's. On a phone channel the reply goes to the number on the other side of the thread.

anyOf.description: Optional key that makes a mailbox send idempotent for the calling key or member. Repeating the request with the same key and body returns the original action in its current state. Keep the key after a lost response. Reusing it with different content returns 409. Active actions retain their key; terminal receipts remain replayable for 24 hours.

post.description: Replies to the sender and every other recipient of the message except the mailbox itself, in the same thread and from the thread's endpoint. A phone thread has one other side, so it answers like a reply.
post.summary: Reply to all recipients of a message

anyOf.description: Optional key that makes a mailbox send idempotent for the calling key or member. Repeating the request with the same key and body returns the original action in its current state. Keep the key after a lost response. Reusing it with different content returns 409. Active actions retain their key; terminal receipts remain replayable for 24 hours.

post.description: Forwards an email to new recipients as a new conversation from the thread's endpoint, with the original quoted below the caller's text and its attachments attached ahead of any the caller adds. The combined attachments must fit the email attachment limits.

get.description: Returns the messages this mailbox holds instead of delivering, most recently held first: suspected spam, phishing, fraud, or prompt injection (`quarantined`), and malware (`isolated`). Each is metadata only; a held message appears in no thread, search, or `mailbox.message.received` event until a person releases it. `after` and `before` filter by when the message was held. Needs `quarantine.read`.

post.description: Delivers a quarantined message into the thread it would have joined and publishes one `mailbox.message.released` event. Releasing it again returns the same result and publishes nothing. Only a person can release; API keys never hold `quarantine.release`. Isolated (malware) messages and discarded messages cannot be released: 409.

Removes a held message from the mailbox's quarantine for good: it leaves the quarantine list, never reaches a thread, and can no longer be released. Quarantined and isolated (malware) messages can both be discarded. Publishes one `mailbox.message.discarded` event; discarding it again returns the same result and publishes nothing. A released message is in its thread and cannot be discarded: 409. Only a person can discard; API keys never hold `quarantine.release`.

get.description: Returns summaries of the caller's unsent drafts in the mailbox, newest first, optionally for one thread. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read a draft's body with `GET /v1/mailboxes/{id}/drafts/{draftId}`.

post.description: Saves a draft of a new message, or of a reply when `inReplyToMessageId` names a message in the mailbox, and returns it with status 201. A phone channel's draft holds a recipient number and text. Send it with `POST /v1/mailboxes/{id}/drafts/{draftId}/send`.

get.description: Returns one of the caller's drafts, or the draft of a send waiting for approval when the caller may approve it.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest; `null` clears an optional field. A draft whose send waits for approval cannot change and conflicts.

delete.description: Discards an unsent draft.

anyOf.description: Optional key that makes a mailbox send idempotent for the calling key or member. Repeating the request with the same key and body returns the original action in its current state. Keep the key after a lost response. Reusing it with different content returns 409. Active actions retain their key; terminal receipts remain replayable for 24 hours.

post.description: Sends one of the caller's drafts: a reply draft in its thread, any other draft as a new conversation. A draft needs recipients, a subject, and a body.

get.description: Returns the actions proposed on a mailbox, newest first, filterable by `threadId`, `state` (`approvalRequired` lists the sends waiting for a person), and creation time (`after`, `before`). Filters apply together within the mailbox. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

Returns one action with its current progress. Send actions expose their immutable approved content, deadline, problem, and accepted receipt. A caller with mailbox read access may inspect actions; send-only callers may inspect only their own proposals. Acceptance and mailbox completion do not mean recipient delivery.

post.description: Cancels a definitely unsent action and reopens its draft atomically. Only an authorized person who proposed the send or can approve actions may cancel. Accepted sends return 409 with their winning receipt and cannot be withdrawn. An uncertain send requires reconciliation and cannot be cancelled as unsent. Cancelling a send held for approval records `resolution.outcome: cancelled` and publishes one `mailbox.action.resolved` event.

Resumes the same action only after its previous execution is confirmed ended and safe continuation is possible. Only an authorized person who proposed the send or can approve actions may retry. Automatic waits need no manual Retry. This does not grant new approval, reset the original deadline, replace the message identity, or resubmit an accepted or uncertain send.

Records approval of a send and returns 202 while it is pending. A send is queued for automatic retry within 15 minutes of approval; repeating approval does not extend this deadline. Accepted, completed, and notSent replays return 200. No expiry applies before approval. Only a person signed in or through OAuth may approve, and never the proposer. Non-send approvals execute synchronously and return 200 with their own execution states. The action's `resolution` names the approver; approving a held send publishes one `mailbox.action.resolved` event.

Denies an action waiting for approval with a reason and returns it without executing it. Only a person signed in or through OAuth may deny, and never the one who proposed it. The action's `resolution` records the denier and reason; denying a held send publishes one `mailbox.action.resolved` event.

get.description: Returns mailbox audit records, newest first, filterable by when they happened (`after`, `before`). Audit event types: `mailbox.created`, `endpoint.attached`, `endpoint.detached`, `message.received`, `message.released`, `message.sent`, `thread.created`, `action.proposed`, `action.policy_decided`, `action.approval_requested`, `action.approval_resolved`, `action.accepted`, `action.executed`, `action.failed`. Thread and draft changes have no dedicated audit event types. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

Returns namespace summaries, newest first, filterable by creation time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read a namespace's metadata with `GET /v1/namespaces/{id}`.

post.description: Creates a namespace with status 201. Names are unique within the organization; a duplicate conflicts.

get.description: Returns one namespace.

patch.description: Updates the fields you name and keeps the rest. `metadata` merges into the stored metadata by key, and a `null` value deletes that key.

delete.description: Deletes an empty namespace. A namespace that still holds anything conflicts, and the error counts what remains: mailboxes, API keys, webhook endpoints filtered to it, domains, senders, contacts, or template projects. Delete each, or return it to organization level with `DELETE /v1/namespaces/{id}/resources/{type}/{resourceId}`; mailboxes, keys, and webhook endpoints cannot move and are deleted. Messages keep the namespace they ran in.

post.description: Moves a resource from organization level or another namespace into this one. A domain brings its senders; a sender on a domain cannot move alone (assign the domain); a contact brings its identities; a template brings every template in its project. A moved resource stops being a default. An address or external id the namespace already holds conflicts. Keys scoped to the old namespace stop reaching the resource at once. Mailboxes, API keys, and webhook endpoints keep the namespace they were created in.
post.summary: Move a resource into a namespace

delete.description: Moves a resource out of this namespace to organization level, with what follows it as in `POST /v1/namespaces/{id}/resources`. A resource in a different namespace is not found.
delete.summary: Return a resource to organization level

get.description: Counts the messages the namespace sent and received in the window that count toward usage, by channel, with the same statuses as `GET /v1/organizations/usage`. A message counts toward the namespace it was sent or received in: that of the sender, mailbox, or key it used. The organization is billed for every namespace; read this to charge your own customer.

Returns the organization's published extensions with their latest version, newest first, filterable by creation time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

post.description: Publishes one version from its manifest and returns it with status 201, creating the extension named by the manifest on its first version. A hosted manifest carries its bundle. Publishing a version again with the same manifest and bundle returns it; a different one conflicts, so bump the manifest's version. Only a person can publish, not an API key.

schema.description: The extension's id (`ext_…`) or its name.

get.description: Returns one extension by its id or name. Its versions are `GET /v1/extensions/{id}/versions`.

schema.description: The extension's id (`ext_…`) or its name.

get.description: Returns summaries of an extension's published versions, newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read a version's manifest with `GET /v1/extensions/{id}/versions/{versionId}`.

schema.description: The extension's id (`ext_…`) or its name.
The version's id (`extver_…`) or its version string, such as `1.0.0`.

get.description: Returns one version, by its id or version string, with the manifest it was published with.

Returns summaries of the organization's extension installations, newest first, filterable by creation time (`after`, `before`). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Read an installation's permissions, scope, and webhook with `GET /v1/extension-installations/{id}`.

post.description: Installs a published version with a scope, permissions, and a send mode, and returns it with status 201. The installation acts on your grants narrowed to these; a webhook installation's API key and webhook secret are returned once. Only a person can install, not an API key.

get.description: Returns one installation with its permissions, scope, send mode, and webhook endpoint.

delete.description: Deletes the installation with its API key and webhook endpoint. Actions it took keep their attribution.

post.description: Changes the pinned version in place. Omit version for the latest publication, or name a version string or id, including an older version to roll back. Preview with dryRun; changing requires acceptPermissions to list exactly the added permission: and event: grants. Only a person can upgrade. Credentials, owner, scope, send mode, and status stay attached to the installation.
post.summary: Upgrade or roll back an installation

post.description: Stops the installation at once: its events stop, and its credential is refused on every surface until it is enabled again.
Resumes a disabled installation. Events published while it was disabled are not delivered.

get.description: Returns the hosted installation's retained handler runs, newest first: outcome, duration, and error. The host keeps the last 100 runs, so the list is bounded and has no cursor. Read a run's logged lines with `GET /v1/extension-installations/{id}/runs/{runId}`.
Returns one retained run with the lines its handler logged: at most 50 lines of 500 characters.

resourceId.description: The resource's id, such as `dom_...` for a domain.

NamespaceMetadata.description: Your own labels for the namespace, such as the id of your customer it serves. Samva stores them and never reads them.

resolution.description: How a held action's approval ended: who approved, denied, or cancelled it, when, and the denial reason. Null while it waits for approval and for an action that never needed one.

reason.description: The denial reason; null for an approval or a cancellation.

resolution.description: How a held action's approval ended: who approved, denied, or cancelled it, when, and the denial reason. Null while it waits for approval and for an action that never needed one.

MailboxChannel.description: The channel an endpoint, thread, or message belongs to.

MailboxSendMode.description: How the grantee's sends execute: `send` runs them within account limits; `approval` holds each one until a different member approves it.

namespaceId.description: Confines the key to one namespace: it reaches only that namespace's domains, senders, numbers, mailboxes, contacts, templates, and messages, never organization-level ones, and only endpoints that confine to a namespace (others answer 403). It holds grants only on `mailboxes`, `messages`, `email`, `domains`, `contacts`, and `templates`. A key scoped to listed mailboxes holds mailbox access only.

permissions.description: `read` reads mailboxes, threads, and messages; `update` changes thread state, labels, drafts, and notes; `send` sends and replies; `quarantine.read` reads quarantined mail.

mailboxIds.description: The mailboxes the key may act on. Omit to reach every mailbox the owner can.

sendMode.description: Defaults to `send`. With `approval`, each send waits until a person other than the key approves it.

message.description: What happened and what you expected, in plain language (at most 4000 characters).

anyOf.description: `bug`: the API behaved wrongly. `confusing`: a response, error, or doc was hard to act on. `missing`: a capability or field you needed does not exist. `other`: anything else.
The operation the report is about, as an SDK method, MCP tool, CLI command, or `METHOD /path` (for example `POST /v1/messages`).
The id of the resource involved, such as a message or domain id.

PhoneRegion.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code, such as US or IN.

slug.description: The brand's handle, unique in the organization; `samva:brand/<slug>` names it.

isDefault.description: Whether bare `samva:brand` and domains without a brand resolve to this brand.

css.description: Brand theme CSS: `@theme` variables, one dark-mode `@theme` of colors, and `@font-face` rules with https WOFF2 sources.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the brand's css, assets and footer. A publication built against a different digest predates the brand's current content.

anyOf.description: Renames the brand. Projects importing `samva:brand/<old slug>` stop building until they import the new slug.

data.description: The input to render with, validated against the publication's input schema.

namespaceId.description: The namespace the template's project belongs to; every entry in a project shares it. Null at organization level. A namespace-scoped key reaches only its own namespace's templates.

digest.description: The brand's digest when the publication was built.

stale.description: Whether the brand has changed since this publication was built. Publishing the same commit again picks up the change.

anyOf.description: With `galleryTemplateId`: whether the new project's `theme.css` imports the organization's default brand (`@import "samva:brand";`) over the starter's look. Defaults to false.

namespaceId.description: The namespace the new template project belongs to; the project and every entry added to it share it. Omit for organization level. A namespace-scoped key always creates in its own namespace.
The namespace the template's project belongs to; every entry in a project shares it. Null at organization level. A namespace-scoped key reaches only its own namespace's templates.

color.description: The list's label color, one of six families, or null for the neutral chip. Customer-chosen and purely presentational; it carries no meaning the API enforces.

email.description: The recipient email address; confirmation proves consent for this address.

from.description: Your verified email sender. The ordinary send pipeline selects its domain and customer brand.

unsubscribeGroupId.description: Clear this unsubscribe group after confirmation; all other opt-outs remain.

anyOf.description: A published email template slug receiving confirmUrl. Omit it to send the default confirmation email.
The recipient IP recorded by your server when they requested subscription.
The signup page or source recorded by your server when consent was requested.

source.description: Where the consent was captured, such as a form URL or a checkout step.

namespaceId.description: The namespace the sender belongs to, or null at organization level. A sender on a domain takes the domain's namespace.

SendsSeries.description: Daily email sends for the last 14 calendar days in the organization's own timezone, oldest first and zero-filled. Always fourteen entries; an entity that has never sent reports fourteen zeroes.

DeliverabilityFacts.description: Bounce and complaint rates over the last 24 hours, as fractions between 0 and 1, with `windowSends`, the deliveries they were divided by, plus `sendingStatus`, which says whether the organization can currently send. The window matches the one the sending-pause rule reads. Below 200 sends that rule ignores the window entirely, so a rate over a smaller `windowSends` is a quotient rather than a reading. These are not a lifetime record; an identity with no traffic in the window reports zeroes.

namespaceId.description: The namespace the domain belongs to, or null at organization level. Only that namespace's keys and organization-wide callers reach it.

sending.description: Whether the domain, the organization, and its sending account are healthy enough to send, as last observed. Ready does not guarantee that a particular send is accepted.

minimumRetainUntil.description: The earliest time the former DKIM record may be removed. Keep it published at least until then so mail signed with the former key still verifies.

namespaceId.description: The namespace the domain belongs to, or null at organization level. Only that namespace's keys and organization-wide callers reach it.

unsubscribeGroupId.description: The unsubscribe group for this send. Omit to inherit the template group; null disables group inheritance for a direct send. Campaigns require a group.

opens.description: Override open tracking for this send. Omit to inherit the organization default. A recipient tracking opt-out always disables tracking.

clicks.description: Override click tracking for this send. Omit to inherit the organization default. A recipient tracking opt-out always disables tracking.

EmailTrackingOverrideV1.description: Requested per-send engagement tracking policy. Recipient opt-out takes precedence, then explicit fields, organization defaults, and product defaults.

unsubscribeGroupId.description: The unsubscribe group for this send. Omit to inherit the template group; null disables group inheritance for a direct send. Campaigns require a group.

tags.description: Messaging analytics, channel stats, and data export. Every date range is half-open — `after` inclusive, `before` exclusive — and may span at most 366 days. Both bounds are absolute ISO-8601 instants carrying `Z` or a numeric offset; a bare calendar date is rejected, because reading it as UTC midnight would shift every bucket for an organization outside UTC. `AnalyticsQueryError` refuses a longer span and a `before` sent without an `after`, which bounds nothing. Omitting both bounds reports the organization's whole history. Calendar buckets follow the organization's timezone.
